column15: And as in the Zohar (Terumah 135a): from the Written Torah we derive the Oral Torah, for the Oral Torah is likewise the aspect of awe. column11: Bava Metzia 107b: ‘And Shmuel says: This term: “All sickness,” refers to the wind. Ruach), and in Eruvin (41b; see Rashi and Tosafot), and other places.

column11: Berakhot 18b: ‘The Gemara challenges this: And is it so that the dead do not know of the pain of others? column11: Berakhot 20a: ‘The Gemara suggests: Let us derive a general principle that human dignity takes precedence over all mitzvot in the Torah from this case. This possibility is rejected: This is a special case, because a case of “sit and refrain from action” [shev ve’al ta’aseh] is different. Engaging in the burial of a met mitzva is not actually in contravention of a mitzva. Rather, by doing so he becomes ritually impure and is then rendered incapable of fulfilling that mitzva. We cannot derive a general principle from here that human dignity would also override a Torah prohibition in a case where that prohibition is directly contravened.’ Context and connection to Sichat Malakhei HaSharet: In Sichat Malakhei HaSharet 4, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and aggadic-halakhic source (Berakhot 20a) to illuminate his exposition here (“and thirteen represents a complete number, being the standard measure employed by our Sages whenever an archetypal tally is required, as noted by Tosafot (Berakhot 20a) and Rashi (Shabbat 119a), for its gematria...”), showing how the translated source sheds light on the nature of the ministering angels, the spiritual elevation of the righteous above the angels through Torah and self-mastery, and the five soul-worlds developed in Sichat Malakhei HaSharet.

column11: Shabbat 119a: ‘The Exilarch said to Rav Hamnuna: What is the meaning of that which is written, “The holy one of God is honored” (Isaiah 58:13)? column11: Sanhedrin 38b: ‘Rabbi Yoḥanan bar Ḥanina says: Daytime is twelve hours long, and the day Adam the first man was created was divided as follows: In the first hour of the day, his dust was gathered. In the sixth, he called the creatures by the names he gave them. In the seventh, Eve was paired with him. In the eighth, they arose to the bed two, and descended four, i.e., Cain and Abel were immediately born. In the ninth, he was commanded not to eat of the Tree of Knowledge. In the tenth, he sinned. column11: Bava Batra 58b: ‘Rabbi Bena’a also saw that it was written there: At the head of all death am I, blood, i.e., people die from an excess of blood; at the head of all life am I, wine, i.e., wine is what gives life. He said to them: If that is so, in the case of someone who falls from a roof and dies, or someone who falls from a palm tree and dies, was it blood that killed him? And furthermore, concerning someone who is on the way to death, can they give him a drink of wine and he will live? Rather, this is what should be written: At the head of all illness am I, blood; at the head of all healing am I, wine. column11: Taanit 7a: ‘Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa raised a contradiction. Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa resolves this apparent contradiction by explaining that if he is a worthy student the teacher must seek him out, as in “to him who is thirsty bring water,” but if the student is not worthy, then “Ho, everyone who thirsts, come for water,” i.e., this student must seek out a teacher himself.’ Context and connection to Sichat Malakhei HaSharet: In Sichat Malakhei HaSharet 4, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and aggadic-halakhic source (Taanit 7a) to illuminate his exposition here (“as I wrote regarding Ta'anit (7a) where Torah is likened to water, wine, and milk: wine alluding specifically to the Oral Torah, welling from the hearts and intellects of Israel's sages. column11: Sanhedrin 91b: ‘And Antoninos said to Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi: From when is the soul placed in a person? column11: Bereshit Rabbah 1:1: ‘Rabbi Hoshaya the Great began: “I was with Him as an amon, a delight day after day…” (Proverbs 8:30) – amon means a child’s caretaker, amon means covered, amon means hidden, and some say amon means greatness. Amon means a child’s caretaker, as it says: “As a caretaker [omen] carries a nursing child” (Numbers 11:12). Amon means covered, as it says: “Those covered [ha’emunim] in scarlet…” (Lamentations 4:5). Amon means hidden, as it says: “He was omen Hadassa” (Esther 2:7). column11: Pesachim 50a: ‘Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: The World-to-Come is not like this world. column11: Tur, Orach Chayim 5:1: ‘5. He should truly intend in the words of his blessings the meaning of the words which come out of his mouth. column11: Berakhot 17a: ‘Rav was wont to say: The World-to-Come is not like this world. In the World-to-Come there is no eating, no drinking, no procreation, no business negotiations, no jealousy, no hatred, and no competition. Rather, the righteous sit with their crowns upon their heads, enjoying the splendor of the Divine Presence, as it is stated: “And they beheld God, and they ate and drank” (Exodus 24:11), meaning that beholding God’s countenance is tantamount to eating and drinking.’ Context and connection to Sichat Malakhei HaSharet: In Sichat Malakhei HaSharet 4, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and aggadic-halakhic source (Berakhot 17a) to illuminate his exposition here (“Whereas in the World to Come it is both written and pronounced, as stated (Berakhot 17a): In the World to Come the righteous sit; sitting everywhere signifying serene rest and the cessation of labor, for commandments...”), showing how the translated source sheds light on the nature of the ministering angels, the spiritual elevation of the righteous above the angels through Torah and self-mastery, and the five soul-worlds developed in Sichat Malakhei HaSharet.

column11: Niddah 61b: ‘The Gemara asks: What is the reason that the halakha is lenient in this case of uncertainty? By Torah law, it is written: “Diverse kinds [sha’atnez]” (Deuteronomy 22:11), and this is interpreted as an acronym indicating that the halakha of diverse kinds does not apply unless the item is combed smooth [shua], spun [tavui] as a thread, and woven [nuz]. Without these characteristics, the combination is not considered diverse kinds by Torah law. And it is the Sages who decreed that diverse kinds that are merely attached to each other are prohibited, despite the fact that they are not combed and spun together. And in this case, since he does not know if it all fell out it is permitted, as the…’ Context and connection to Sichat Malakhei HaSharet: In Sichat Malakhei HaSharet 4, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and aggadic-halakhic source (Niddah 61b) to illuminate his exposition here (“sitting everywhere signifying serene rest and the cessation of labor, for commandments are obsolete in the future era (Niddah 61b). column13: And for this reason teshuvah does not avail to exempt [one] from the punishments of the [earthly] court — which [would work] by uprooting the deed retroactively — for through teshuvah it is “as if he did not sin,” and the willful sins become as unwitting ones, or as merits — so why should he be punished? column11: Shabbat 55a: ‘And that is the meaning of that which is written: “Slay utterly old and young, both maid, and little children, and women; but come not near any man upon whom is the mark; and begin at My Sanctuary” (Ezekiel 9:6). column11: Berakhot 20a: ‘Abaye said to Rav Pappa: The previous generations were wholly dedicated to the sanctification of God’s name, while we are not as dedicated to the sanctification of God’s name. Since he thought that she was Jewish, he stood and ripped it from her. It was then divulged that she was a non-Jew and he was taken to court due to the shame that he caused her, and they assessed the payment for the shame that he caused her at four hundred zuz. Ultimately,…’ Context and connection to Sichat Malakhei HaSharet: In Sichat Malakhei HaSharet 4, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and aggadic-halakhic source (Berakhot 20a) to illuminate his exposition here (“But in the realm of practical action, on the contrary, the Sages stated (Berakhot 20a): "Patience, patience is worth four hundred zuz" [understand the mystical significance of the number four hundred, which denotes...”), showing how the translated source sheds light on the nature of the ministering angels, the spiritual elevation of the righteous above the angels through Torah and self-mastery, and the five soul-worlds developed in Sichat Malakhei HaSharet.
column13: But the measure of "two doorways" applies to every person, for every entity is structured of two that are four—namely two polar opposites, it being impossible for any reality to lack two extremities. And they are four: two extremities, the balancing center, and the fourth corporeal vessel encompassing them. Therefore: "Deliberate, deliberate is worth four hundred zuz twice over" (Berakhot 20a)—meaning four times the orders of one hundred where deliberation resides, within the mind and heart alluded to by the number hundred, as I wrote elsewhere.
column15: The explanation is as stated in the Holy Zohar (Bereishit 24b), that the worlds are arranged like the layers of an onion: meaning that each world is an outer garment for the realm above it, this physical world being a garment for the supernal world, ascending higher and higher to the Infinite.

column15: As taught in the Holy Zohar (Bereishit 16a): Darkness is fire, etc., and this is the mystery of (Genesis 27:1) “and his eyes were dim from seeing”; and in Zohar (Toldot 142a): “‘And the darkness He called Night’—this is Isaac, who drew the night into himself, etc., seeking to envelop himself in awe and cleave to his designated rung, whereupon the night bound itself to him, fulfilling ‘and the darkness He called Night.’”

Nonetheless, it occurred to him on account of the toil of the journey which was for a mitzvah; and behold, "he who keeps a commandment shall know no evil thing" (Ecclesiastes 8:5), and this is termed "evil," as is known.
column15: “I remember for you the devotion of your youth, the love of your espousals, how you walked after Me in the wilderness, in an unsown land” (Jeremiah 2:2). When a person stands in serene clarity of mind, it is easy to recognize that God governs all; the true test and preciousness of Israel’s service is when a person’s mind is constricted in the ‘unsown wilderness’ of confusion, yet he continues to walk loyally after the Blessed Name.

column15: “And shall pitch it within and without with pitch”—this counsel was given corresponding to “and one who forgives his grievances”: meaning that he must pardon his fellow within and without, free of duplicity; not like Absalom saying “Amnon your brother,” which was mere lip service while hatred remained concealed in his heart; and unlike Joseph’s brothers of whom it is said “and could not speak peaceably unto him,” refusing to speak deceitfully.

column15: “Heaven” corresponds to the power of pure thought, and “throne” signifies spiritual certainty. The meaning is: in the realm of inward contemplation man has security that he will not swerve from His will, for as long as a matter remains in thought, he retains free will to restrain his impulse before it manifests, and furthermore, man is not punished for unacted thought.

column11: Bereshit Rabbah 10:6: ‘Bar Sira said: God produced drugs from the earth with which the physician heals the wound, and with which the pharmacist mixes his compounds.38:4. column13: Showing clearly that Unity does not signify contemplating His Essence as being devoid of multiplicity and change as posited by Chovot HaLevavot, Maimonides, and their school, for upon that aspect applies only the negative command "Take heed...", whereas it has no bearing upon faith in Divinity whose core is Divine Providence, as written in Section 1, which stands opposite negative theology; and in truth, those who philosophized regarding faith through stripping away corporeality and accidents came to deny Providence, reward, punishment, and responsiveness to prayer and human deeds, denying the essence of the Torah.

column15: “… and why do you raise yourselves above the community of God?” (Bamidbar, 16:3)Here Korach’s assertion was that there is no favoritism in Israel, that God doesn’t elevate one above the other, for God dwells among them all equally. This is similar to what is said in the Midrash (Gemara Ta’anit, 31a), “In the future God will make a circle dance of the righteous, and all will point to God saying, ‘this is our God whom we have hoped for.’”

column11: Jerusalem Talmud Sheviit 9:1: ‘.rabba 79(6), Eccl.rabbati 10(11), [Pesiqta dRav Cahana ed. S. Buber p. 886; added from Addenda and Corrigenda by Guggenehimer], Babli Šabbat 33b–34a. column15: And for this reason, in the generation of King Hezekiah and the generation of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai a rainbow was never seen in their lifetimes (Bereishit Rabbah 35:2); because they embodied the connective Vav, illuminating through their deeds so that such dense darkness never enveloped the world, rendering the sign of the rainbow unnecessary.

column15: As taught in the Holy Zohar (Bereishit 22a): When He arrived at the world of division, which is the world of separated entities, the Artisan said to the Master of the building: “Let us make man”; meaning, once all creations were isolated and divided from one another, lacking communion, the Blessed Name said: “Let us make man,” who would possess the faculty of speech, uniting all creations through his prayer and divine service unto Hashem.

column13: And Jacob's truth—the root of divine Truth cast down into this deceptive world (Bereishit Rabbah 8)—was proven when he told Isaac: "I am Esau your firstborn," which superficially appeared untruthful, yet was the very moment he inherited the blessings of "And God give you," expounded as "He will grant you His Divinity," perceiving Hashem before his eyes as the sole Sovereign within everything bestowed upon him; flowing from his attribute of Truth—the seal of the Holy One (Shabbat 55a)—whose visage is etched on the Throne of Glory (Chullin 91b).
column15: For among the heavenly hosts His greatness is not so remarkably evident, since they lack moral choice, and “whither the spirit was to go, they went” (Ezekiel 1:12); it is specifically within the realm of separated multiplicity, where the nations exist acting in total opposition and denying the power of Hashem, that the Blessed Name formed the human archetype—the core of which is Israel, who consciously coronate the Blessed Name over themselves.

column13: And so is all wisdom of their sages in this world, for nothing is termed "wisdom" other than the perception of truth; for falsehood is not wisdom, but deceitful imagination, being in truth folly; and the wise men of Haman, who possessed profound worldly wisdom, recognized the greatness of the seed of the Jews and that Haman was doomed to fall; reaching this conclusion at the very end when his downfall was imminent, having already begun in deed; it being poised for completion, requiring no profound prophetic Da'as of the hidden.
column15: Thus we find that all majesty and glory emerge solely through the power of divine concealment. And man through his dedicated service attains perception of the light of the Blessed Name. Yet this occurs within the dynamic of “running and returning” (ratzo va-shov), wherein the light touches and touches not (mati ve-la mati), as taught in the Holy Zohar (Bereishit 16b).

column15: From which it is proven that the Commander Himself is endless and boundless, and His glory fills the entire universe. column15: “Brethren, neither sackcloth nor fasting brings atonement; rather, repentance and good deeds bring atonement, for so we find concerning the men of Nineveh: it is not written ‘And God saw their sackcloth and their fasting,’ but ‘And God saw their deeds, that they turned from their evil way’ (Jonah 3:10)” (Taanit 16a). Fasting and bodily affliction are only preparatory instruments to humble the heart; the essence desired by the Blessed Name is the inward turning of the heart and the rectification of one’s deeds.

column13: Therefore it is stated: "the whole earth is full of His glory", for 'the earth' is this physical world wherein revelation occurs strictly via garments— which is merely His manifest glory; and "man shall not see Me and live", for the transcendent divine Essence cannot be unveiled in this world at all. And likewise Israel in this world: "their secrets are concealed", in that their essence is not exposed, but only the outward garments; for the essence of Israel cleaves unto Hashem, blessed be He.

And that is: for the human soul hewn from Above desires continually to ascend to its celestial source and not turn toward this world which is entirely material; yet when shown that Hashem's glory fills the earth, no place being void of Him.

column15: In truth, with the Blessed Name there is no change; change exists only from man’s side: when mortals sin, the divine garments are stripped away, as stated in the Zohar (Bereishit 23b): “Whoever sins is as if he stripped the Shechinah of Her garments.”

column13: For the general emotional attributes divide into two, corresponding to the two opposite poles of Chesed [kindness] and Gevurah [severity], from whose dross are drawn the two inclinations of envy and lust, which are opposites: for one who is inclined toward desire is sociable and benevolent toward creatures; and this is found among the nations, where to outward appearances there are individuals who possess a generous eye and affection toward people; and this is the purpose of the mitzvah of Mishloach Manot: to demonstrate that true altruistic benevolence exists in truth only within Israel alone.
column15: For true unity flourishes only when dedicated to Heavenly honor, Hashem guaranteeing that within every gathering for Heaven’s sake His presence dwells, as in Avot (3:6): “Even two who sit and engage in Torah, the Shechinah rests between them”; while the gathering of the wicked is dispersion, as in Sanhedrin (26a): “A conspiracy of the wicked is not counted.”

column11: Pesachim 56a: ‘We learned in the mishna that the residents of Jericho would bundle Shema. The Gemara asks: What does it mean that they bundled Shema? How did they do so? This baraita teaches that the angels mention the name of God only after three words, i.e., after saying the word “holy” three times, whereas according to what Rav Ḥananel stated that Rav said, the third group of angels says the word “holy” once and then immediately mentions the name of God.’ Context and connection to Sichat Malakhei HaSharet: In Sichat Malakhei HaSharet 4, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and aggadic-halakhic source (Chullin 91b) to illuminate his exposition here (“[whereby the difficulty raised by Tosafot in Chullin 91b is resolved—their answer remaining incomplete as to why the Gemara specified only the Ophanim and not the Chayot; for according to our exposition, the...”), showing how the translated source sheds light on the nature of the ministering angels, the spiritual elevation of the righteous above the angels through Torah and self-mastery, and the five soul-worlds developed in Sichat Malakhei HaSharet.

column11: Zohar, Terumah: ‘The answer is indicated by the verse: “He maketh his angels spirits, his ministers a flaming fire” (Ps. 104, 4). The first of these categories are those angels that stand outside while the second are those that stand within the innermost circle. Now those who encounter the serpent are “spirits”, and that serpent is a spirit also. The spirit of impurity does not mingle with the spirit of holiness, and therefore those angels that are called “spirits” cannot enter into the Holy Presence because of that spirit of impurity. Those angels, however, which are within are “fire”, and that supernal holy fire ejects the impurity so that it cannot enter into the innermost place.
